entries.title: Signed-out bounce after a sign-in that looked successful
entries.recognize: The URL leaves the sign-in page, then the screen returns to a sign-in or landing page within seconds, and every later step reports nothing found.
entries.tell: No authenticated-area control (member search, sign-out, operator banner) ever appeared, and the URL went back to sign-in with no navigation by the driver.
mistaken_for: A member with no accounts or statements
entries.probe: Record every URL the browser passes through for several seconds after the submit, and look for an authenticated-area control on the screen, not just a changed URL.
entries.recover: Treat the run as not signed in, stop, and return a typed sign-in failure; never report an empty success. If a fresh browser took an "already signed in" shortcut, that shortcut is the defect.
approaches: Positive sign-in proof
Poll for content, not the URL or load event
entries.prevent: A sign-in is proven only by an authenticated-area control on a stable screen, never by a URL change alone.
entries.hazard: proposed: a hand-off that briefly draws the console, then returns to the sign-in page

entries.title: Real sign-in judged failed because the landing screen was unexpected
entries.recognize: The screenshot shows the signed-in console while the driver still waits for a sign-in field or raises a navigation error.
entries.tell: The screen holds authenticated-area controls, but the landing differs from the one the driver checks for: a trusted-workstation landing, an interstitial, or another host or path.
entries.probe: Record the landing screen of a signed-in session from a fresh browser and from a trusted workstation, and test each against the driver's success check.
entries.recover: Base the success check on authenticated-area controls that every landing shares, then re-run from a fresh sign-in.
approaches: Positive sign-in proof
Scout the live screen before writing targets
entries.prevent: The success check names controls of the authenticated area, not one URL, and is tested against every known landing.
entries.hazard: Trusted-workstation "Welcome back" sign-in, followed by the promotional interstitial

entries.title: Acting while the sign-in hand-off is still in flight
entries.recognize: The driver's next step runs while the sign-in form, a spinner or a blank callback page is still on screen, and the next screen bounces back to sign-in.
entries.tell: The driver acted within a moment of the submit, or while the URL was still on the sign-in or callback page.
entries.probe: Log the time and URL at the submit and at the driver's next action, and whether the hand-off page was still showing.
entries.recover: Wait for positive proof of sign-in before any navigation; a callback page is mid-sign-in, not signed in.
approaches: Positive sign-in proof
Poll for content, not the URL or load event
entries.prevent: No navigation is allowed between the password submit and positive proof of sign-in.
entries.hazard: Slow hand-off

entries.title: List frame drawn with zero rows behind a step-up code prompt
entries.recognize: The statements or activity screen shows its header, filters and table frame with no rows, and every period reads unavailable.
entries.tell: A verification or code prompt sits elsewhere on the screen or in another frame, and the screen's own empty-state wording is absent.
entries.probe: Read every frame and shadow root for verify, identity or code wording, and compare with the screen's own empty-state wording.
entries.recover: Treat it as a code step: confirm the code was sent, hand back for a person to supply it, and never report the list as empty.
approaches: Handle a step-up code after sign-in
Read through shadow roots
Confirmed-send invariant
entries.prevent: Zero rows counts as empty only when the screen's own empty-state wording is present.
entries.hazard: proposed: a step-up staff code demanded inside the main frame before the statements table fills

entries.title: Promotional interstitial in place of the expected screen
entries.recognize: The expected list or summary never appears; the main frame holds a promotion, an upsell or an enrollment prompt.
entries.tell: The frame holds promotional or "set up later" wording with a dismiss control such as "Not now".
entries.probe: Take a screenshot, list every frame with its URL, and look for dismiss wording such as "Not now", "Later" or "No thanks".
entries.recover: Press the dismiss control only, never "Learn more" or an enrollment control, then wait for the expected screen to be fully rendered.
approaches: Dismiss interstitials without enrolling
Read the right frame
Handle splash, gate and consent pages
entries.prevent: Dismissal accepts only controls whose names decline or defer; a control that enrolls or accepts an offer is refused.
entries.hazard: Promotional interstitial

entries.title: Acknowledgement or consent gate blocks the flow
entries.recognize: A screen shows none of the expected fields, or a correctly filled form does nothing on submit, and no error appears.
entries.tell: An accept or acknowledge control, or an unchecked required checkbox, is on the screen, and the flow advances only once it is used.
entries.probe: Look for a disclaimer or terms screen with an acknowledge control, and list unchecked required checkboxes and disabled submits in every frame.
entries.recover: Acknowledge only a notice the tenant profile allows the driver to accept; otherwise hand back for a person to decide.
approaches: Handle splash, gate and consent pages
entries.prevent: Each acknowledgement the driver may press is listed in the tenant profile; an unlisted gate is an unknown screen.
entries.hazard: Bank 3's "Terms updated: Acknowledge" page after sign-in

entries.title: Every period yields the same document, or the wrong one
entries.recognize: Distinct periods return the same row text, the same file or the same verdict; statements land under the wrong year; or rows are skipped as empty though each one opens a real document.
entries.tell: Distinct periods give identical bytes, or the key used to match a row repeats across groups or carries a flag the document contradicts.
entries.probe: Hash every retrieved file and compare across periods, and list the keys rows were matched on to look for repeats across groups.
entries.recover: Choose each row by its visible identity (statement date, account ending digits) read from the screen, never by position, element id or a summary row, and re-scout the list.
approaches: Scout the live screen before writing targets
File by the statement date inside the PDF
entries.prevent: Distinct periods must give distinct bytes; a run that returns one hash for several periods fails.
entries.hazard: proposed: a static "Most recent statement" summary row above the statement table, with the same Statement button

entries.title: Hidden duplicate field or button
entries.recognize: The driver waits on the credential field or the submit and times out the same way on every retry, though the control is plainly on the screen.
entries.tell: The bound control is hidden, and a visible control with the same role and name comes later in document order.
entries.probe: List every match for the control with its visibility and position on the screen, and check which one the driver bound.
entries.recover: Target only visible controls present in the screen model, and re-target when the control moves.
approaches: Visible-only targets
Click the named control by accessible role and name
entries.prevent: Targets resolve only among visible controls; a target that matches more than one visible control fails loudly.
entries.hazard: proposed: a hidden copy of the password field and Sign In button earlier in document order

entries.title: Loose match binds the wrong visible control
entries.recognize: The driver lands on a help, other-sign-in or settings screen instead of submitting, or a code is typed into a username or phone field.
entries.tell: The bound control's name only contains the expected word, or its field hints suggest a code while it is another field, and the sign-in form is still on the screen.
entries.probe: List every button and field with its accessible name, type and hints, and check which one the driver bound and what screen followed.
entries.recover: Match controls by exact accessible name and role within the expected region, and accept a code field only once the screen's code wording is present.
approaches: Click the named control by accessible role and name
Visible-only targets
Confirmed-send invariant
entries.prevent: Control names are matched exactly, never by substring, and a code field counts only on a screen that says a code was sent.
entries.hazard: proposed: a "Sign In Help" link beside "Sign In", and a member-number field marked as a one-time-code input

entries.title: Typed value not registered by the page's script
entries.recognize: Credentials or an amount appear entered, but the submit never enables, or the application rejects the entry with its own wording.
entries.tell: The rejection wording belongs to the application, and entering the value as real key events into an enabled field changes the outcome.
entries.probe: Check whether the submit or the next field enables only after key events, and compare a value set directly with one typed key by key on the same screen.
entries.recover: Wait until the field is editable, type the value as key events, and read the value back before submitting.
approaches: Wait until a field is editable
Type with real key events
Robust text entry past a length limit
entries.prevent: Every text entry is followed by a read-back of the field's value before any submit.
entries.hazard: proposed: a field whose script copies its value only on key events, so a value set without typing is lost

entries.title: Returning-workstation layout hides the username field
entries.recognize: The username field is never found, the same way on every retry, only from a browser that has signed in before.
entries.tell: It fails only with a stored profile; a fresh browser shows the username field.
mistaken_for: A portal that refuses the browser
entries.probe: Compare a fresh and a returning scout of the sign-in screen: is the username prefilled, hidden or behind a "Not you?" control?
entries.recover: Handle both layouts in the driver, or use the "Not you?" or "use a different user" control to reach the full form.
approaches: Handle the returning-user layout
Clear the stored profile to force a fresh sign-in
entries.prevent: Every sign-in driver is tested against both the fresh and the returning layout.
entries.hazard: Trusted-workstation "Welcome back" sign-in page

entries.title: Sign-in takes a different path after the first step
entries.recognize: After the first credential step the expected next field never appears; the screen shows a code field, or the console itself.
entries.tell: The expected field is absent, and another known screen (code entry, the console) is present.
entries.probe: After each sign-in step, wait for any of the known next screens and record which one appeared on each run.
entries.recover: Branch on the screen that actually appeared; treat each known branch as a valid path and anything else as an unknown screen.
approaches: Adaptive one- or two-step sign-in
entries.prevent: After each sign-in step the driver waits on the set of known next screens, not on one expected field.
entries.hazard: Trusted-workstation cookie that skips the staff code step

entries.title: Content arrives after the page looks loaded
entries.recognize: "Not found" or "layout changed" is raised within a second of navigation, while the failure screenshot shows the very row the driver said was absent.
entries.tell: The screenshot shows the row the driver reported missing.
entries.probe: Compare the failure time with the navigation time, and poll for the row with a budget, logging when it first appears.
entries.recover: Wait until the screen is fully rendered and the expected content is present, within a time limit, before judging anything absent.
approaches: Poll for content, not the URL or load event
Never wait for network idle
entries.prevent: No absence verdict is allowed before the screen is fully rendered and a content wait has used its budget.
entries.hazard: Late rows

entries.title: Network idle never arrives on a busy page
entries.recognize: A wait times out, or uses its whole budget, on a screen that is visibly rendered.
entries.tell: The network shows steady polling or beacon traffic, and the screen was ready long before the wait ended.
entries.probe: Record requests during the wait, and check which condition the driver waited on.
entries.recover: Wait for specific content on the screen instead of network silence.
approaches: Never wait for network idle
Poll for content, not the URL or load event
entries.prevent: Drivers never wait on network idle; readiness is defined by content on the screen.
entries.hazard: proposed: a keep-alive or message poll every second from the console's banner frame

entries.title: Effective time limit differs from the one asked for
entries.recognize: A run sits waiting for many minutes without failing, or a wait that asked for longer ends early at a default.
entries.tell: The wait that ended is not the one the driver asked for: an inherited ceiling far above the step's need, or an inner default capping a longer outer wait.
mistaken_for: A portal slower than the wait
entries.probe: Log the effective time limit of each wait beside the value the caller passed, including inner waits under an outer deadline.
entries.recover: Give every step an explicit time limit sized to its need, under a wall-clock deadline for the whole task.
approaches: Bound every per-item loop with a deadline
Poll for content, not the URL or load event
entries.prevent: Every wait states its own time limit, and no inner wait may exceed the remaining task deadline.
entries.hazard: Slow hand-off

entries.title: Opening a document navigates away from the list
entries.recognize: The first document is retrieved; every later one is reported missing from the list almost at once.
entries.tell: The first retrieval succeeds and the rest fail faster than any screen could load.
entries.probe: Log the URL and the screen before and after the first retrieval, and check whether the list is still on screen.
entries.recover: Return to the list, wait for it to be fully rendered, and re-target each row by identity before the next retrieval.
approaches: Reopen the list after each download
Adopt new windows and popups
entries.prevent: After any retrieval the driver re-reads the screen before acting again.
entries.hazard: proposed: one tenant's Statement button replaces the main frame with the PDF instead of opening a window

entries.title: Delivery chooser sends nothing until a channel is chosen
entries.recognize: A person is asked for a code that never arrives; the screen shows a channel chooser and no code field.
entries.tell: There is no code field and no "we sent a code" wording after the chooser.
entries.probe: Look for the portal's own send acknowledgement or a code field, and for channel buttons still on the screen.
entries.recover: Pick the channel the tenant profile names, wait for the send acknowledgement, and only then ask the person for the code.
approaches: Confirmed-send invariant
Pick the delivery channel in the chooser
entries.prevent: A person is asked for a code only after the screen confirms one was sent.
entries.hazard: Staff code chooser page (text or email)

entries.title: Click reported done but nothing happened
entries.recognize: A press on a visible control returns without error and nothing follows: no request, no new screen, no download; on a code screen the form is still present.
entries.tell: No request reached the server, and the form or screen is unchanged.
entries.probe: Watch the network for a request after the press, and check whether the screen changed or the form went away.
entries.recover: Verify the effect of every press; if there is none, re-target and press once more only when the action is safe to repeat. On a code screen, never request a new code.
approaches: A click is not proof
Never send again; wait for the code form to detach
entries.prevent: Every press is followed by a check for its expected effect, and a code submit without effect is never answered with a resend.
entries.hazard: Swallowed click

entries.title: Code form still on screen after an accepted code
entries.recognize: A second code is requested for a code that already worked.
entries.tell: The code form is detaching or the hand-off is starting, and the duplicate request came right after the submit.
entries.probe: Compare the time of the duplicate request with the submit, and check whether the form is leaving the screen.
entries.recover: Wait for the code form to go away or for an error message; never request a second code.
approaches: Never send again; wait for the code form to detach
Detect a silent code rejection
entries.prevent: A code challenge is raised at most once per sign-in unless the screen shows a rejection message.
entries.hazard: proposed: the code form stays drawn for a few seconds after an accepted code, before the hand-off

entries.title: Code expired before it was submitted
entries.recognize: After a code is submitted the code field stays, often with no error wording, or the person saw the prompt long after the code was sent.
entries.tell: The code's age at submit exceeds the portal's expiry, or the prompt reached the person late, queued behind another challenge.
mistaken_for: A portal that rejects good codes
entries.probe: Compare when the code was sent, when the person saw the prompt and when it was submitted, and wait past the detach window to see whether the field stays.
entries.recover: Return a typed code-expired result and hand back; do not request another code within the run.
approaches: Detect a silent code rejection
Durable code challenge with one owner
entries.prevent: A code prompt reaches the person as soon as the send is confirmed and shows how long the code has left.
entries.hazard: proposed: a tenant that clears the code field with no message when the code has expired

entries.title: A code is demanded on every sign-in
entries.recognize: Every run asks for a fresh code, and codes pile up in the inbox when sign-in is retried, each one replacing the last.
entries.tell: The trusted-workstation cookie is absent or was not kept between runs, or the tenant asks for a code on every sign-in by design.
entries.probe: Count codes received per run, and check whether the trusted-workstation cookie survived from the last run.
entries.recover: Persist the trusted-workstation cookie per tenant, and never retry a sign-in that has reached the code step.
approaches: Persist the trusted-workstation cookie
Post-submit failures are terminal
entries.prevent: A sign-in that reached the code step is never retried automatically.
entries.hazard: Staff code step on every sign-in without a trusted-workstation cookie

entries.title: Relative document link resolved against the wrong base
entries.recognize: Every document retrieval fails with an invalid-URL error in production and the run reports no statements, while tests passed.
entries.tell: The link is relative, and the test context supplied a base URL that production does not.
entries.probe: Read the link as the screen gives it, and check whether it has a scheme and host.
entries.recover: Resolve every link against the URL of the frame it came from, or open it by acting on the control on the screen.
approaches: Fetch the document URL within the signed-in session
Take the URL from a link on the screen
entries.prevent: Links are resolved against their own frame's URL, and tests run without a default base URL.
entries.hazard: Per-tenant URL shapes (path prefix, bare port, numeric host)

entries.title: Document bytes arrive without a download
entries.recognize: Pressing the document control fires no download and exposes no link, or a response is plainly there but its body reads empty.
entries.tell: A PDF response crosses the wire, into a new window, a popup or a built-in viewer, while no download event fires.
entries.probe: Record every response with its content type while the control is pressed, and note any new window and what it loaded.
entries.recover: Read the document from where it arrived: adopt the new window, capture the PDF response, and check that the bytes start with the PDF header.
approaches: Adopt new windows and popups
Capture PDF responses at the context level
Turn a download event into bytes
Intercept a response before the built-in viewer consumes it
entries.prevent: Document retrieval goes through one shared helper that handles downloads, new windows and viewer responses, and checks the PDF header.
entries.hazard: Statement button opens the PDF in a new window

entries.title: Document answers HTML, not a PDF
entries.recognize: The document request returns an HTML viewer, an error shell or undecoded bytes, or a printed copy of an HTML statement is cut off at the edge.
entries.tell: The bytes do not start with the PDF header, while the document opens in the browser, a sibling returns a PDF, or the viewer has its own Download control.
entries.probe: Record the status, content type and first bytes of every document response, and look for a Download control on the HTML page.
entries.recover: Use the viewer's own Download control when it exists; print to PDF only when no PDF exists, then check that the printed text is not clipped.
approaches: Capture PDF responses at the context level
Fetch the document URL within the signed-in session
Print an HTML document to PDF
entries.prevent: A saved document must start with the PDF header; anything else is a typed error, never a success.
entries.hazard: proposed: one tenant's statement window shows an HTML viewer with its own Download button

entries.title: Replaying the page's request outside the page is refused
entries.recognize: A document or data request seen in the page fails when the driver sends it directly, though the page loads the same data.
entries.tell: The page's own request succeeds, while the replay is refused, needs a value that changes every session, or returns an unreadable body.
entries.probe: Compare the page's request with the replay field by field, and capture the same request in a second session to see what changes.
entries.recover: Stop replaying; act on the screen and read the document from the window or response where it arrived.
approaches: Capture PDF responses at the context level
Adopt new windows and popups
entries.prevent: Drivers act through the screen and never hand-build requests to a portal's private endpoints.
entries.hazard: proposed: the statement request needs a per-window token, so a request sent outside the opened window is refused

entries.title: Requested periods do not line up with real statement dates
entries.recognize: Every period in a fixed recent window reads unavailable, or one period gets two documents while a neighbor reads empty.
entries.tell: The list shows real dates outside the window, or the date printed in the PDF differs from the row date the period was matched on.
entries.probe: Read the actual statement dates on the list before requesting periods, and compare each PDF's printed statement date with its row date.
entries.recover: Enumerate real document dates first, then file each document by the statement date printed inside it.
approaches: Enumerate real document dates first
File by the statement date inside the PDF
entries.hazard: proposed: a member with quarterly statements, and a row date that is the posting date rather than the statement date

entries.title: Notices mixed in with statements
entries.recognize: Some retrieved documents are marked failed because they hold no transactions, and a real but nearly empty statement is marked failed too.
entries.tell: The document is a notice, a tax form or a blank page, so zero transactions is the right answer.
entries.probe: Open the documents that yielded no rows, and read their titles and the list's document type column.
entries.recover: Select documents by their type on the list and inside the PDF, and keep a statement with no activity as a valid statement.
approaches: File by the statement date inside the PDF
entries.prevent: Document type is checked before a document is judged.
entries.hazard: proposed: privacy notices and tax forms listed in the statements table under Document Type

entries.title: Paged list hides older periods
entries.recognize: Recent periods are found and older ones read unavailable, though the list has later pages or more rows below.
entries.tell: A pager or "View more" control is present, and every missing period is older than every found one.
entries.probe: Look for a pager or "View more" control, and compare the oldest date on the screen with the oldest period requested.
entries.recover: Page or expand the list until the oldest requested period is reached or the list ends, within a time limit.
approaches: Operate pagers, accordions and pickers to reveal rows
Bound every per-item loop with a deadline
entries.hazard: proposed: the statement table shows twelve rows with a "View more statements" link

entries.title: Rows load only after an expand or a selection
entries.recognize: The list container renders empty until an account is picked or a section is expanded, and a picker choice may land on a different item.
entries.tell: The container stays empty however long the driver waits, and fills only after a picker or section control is used.
entries.probe: Wait past the late-content budget, then list the controls that fill the list, and read back the selection after each pick.
entries.recover: Operate the picker or section control, read back the displayed selection, and wait for the rows to be fully rendered.
approaches: Operate pagers, accordions and pickers to reveal rows
A click is not proof
entries.prevent: Every picker choice is read back from the screen before the driver relies on it.
entries.hazard: Statements page account picker

entries.title: Statements offered only as options of one picker
entries.recognize: No statement rows or links are on the statements screen; it holds one picker whose options are closing dates.
entries.tell: One picker's option labels are dates, often with a two-digit year, and its values are opaque ids.
mistaken_for: A download control that does nothing
entries.probe: List every picker on the screen with its option labels, and the form and button it belongs to.
entries.recover: Choose each option by its date label, submit the form, read the document from where it arrives, and parse two-digit years with care.
approaches: Submit the statement form for each option
Operate pagers, accordions and pickers to reveal rows
entries.hazard: proposed: one tenant lists statements as options of a single picker with a View button that posts the form

entries.title: Row menu drawn outside the row
entries.recognize: The document is listed but never retrieved, and a search inside the row finds no menu items.
entries.tell: The row's menu opens on screen, but its items are drawn elsewhere on the page, outside the row.
mistaken_for: A document that cannot be downloaded
entries.probe: Open the row's menu and look for its items across the whole screen, not inside the row.
entries.recover: Target the menu items by name across the whole screen right after opening the menu, and confirm they belong to that row's menu.
approaches: Scout the live screen before writing targets
Visible-only targets
entries.hazard: proposed: a per-row Options menu whose items are drawn at the end of the page, outside the row

entries.title: Wrong or partial account coverage
entries.recognize: Only one account's results come back though the member has several, results land under the wrong account, or the screen holds no accounts at all.
entries.tell: Several account tiles are on the screen and the driver took the first, or the scope shown on the screen (member, account ending digits) does not match the task.
entries.probe: List every account tile with its ending digits, compare them with the task's account, and check the member shown in the banner.
entries.recover: Choose the account by its identity on the screen, never by position; when the task names no account and several match, fail loudly with a typed error.
approaches: Enumerate every account with a stable reference
Pick by identity hint, else fail loudly
Check every scope the sign-in can reach
entries.prevent: Accounts are chosen by identity read from the screen; choosing by position is refused.
entries.hazard: proposed: account tiles drawn in a different order on each load

entries.title: Direct navigation to a guessed or stored URL
entries.recognize: After a direct load of a deep URL the session ends, or the screen shows an empty view, the home screen or a not-found page while still signed in.
entries.tell: The direct load failed while the console's own menu reaches the screen, and the on-screen link carries a session value the guessed URL lacks.
entries.probe: From the authenticated landing, follow the console's own menu to the screen, and compare each URL with the guessed one.
entries.recover: Navigate through links and menus on the screen, taking each URL from the screen as rendered, never from a guess.
approaches: Take the URL from a link on the screen
Preserve session tokens in URLs
Scout the live screen before writing targets
entries.prevent: Drivers take every URL from the tenant profile or from a link on the screen; a hand-written deep URL is refused.
entries.hazard: proposed: inner frame URLs carry a per-session token, and a load without it ends the session

entries.title: Session expires mid-run
entries.recognize: A run that works when watched fails unattended; partway through, the sign-in screen appears where the work should be.
entries.tell: The failure comes after a fixed idle or session lifetime, whatever the driver did.
entries.probe: Compare the session's start time and the tenant's idle limit with the time of failure, and look for a warning dialog before it.
entries.recover: Read the sign-in screen inside the work frame as session expiry, stop with a typed result, and start a fresh sign-in only if the task allows it.
approaches: Positive sign-in proof
Persistent profile as the primary session
entries.prevent: Every screen check includes a session-expired check, so expiry is never read as an empty result.
entries.hazard: Session warning and expiry

entries.title: Repeated attempts turn a rejection into a lockout
entries.recognize: Rejections escalate across attempts: first a plain rejection, then a lockout or a cap on codes.
entries.tell: The escalation follows the number and spacing of recent attempts, and the first attempt behaved differently.
mistaken_for: A new, harder barrier to work around
entries.probe: Read the attempt record for this tenant and operator: the count and spacing of recent sign-ins.
entries.recover: Stop, cool down and hand back; never retry a password submit automatically.
approaches: Hard attempt cap per account
Post-submit failures are terminal
Cooldown instead of retry
Single supervised attempt
entries.prevent: One password submit per run; a rejection after the submit ends the run with a typed error.
entries.hazard: Operator lockout after too many sign-in attempts

entries.title: Stored credential is stale
entries.recognize: Every attempt is rejected right after the submit with the same generic wording, while the fields hold exactly the stored values.
entries.tell: A person typing the stored value in a normal browser gets the same rejection.
entries.probe: Prove the field contents match the stored value by length without printing them, and ask a person to sign in once with the stored value.
entries.recover: Stop after one rejection, hand back for the credential to be updated, and spend no repair effort on the driver.
approaches: Classify before repairing
Post-submit failures are terminal
Hard attempt cap per account
entries.prevent: A credential rejection is classified before any driver repair begins.
entries.hazard: Bad-credentials message with a stale stored password

entries.title: Tenant profile points at the wrong portal
entries.recognize: Valid credentials are rejected, or the sign-in works and the expected screens are not where the driver looks.
entries.tell: The credential's own sign-in URL, or the branding on the screen, names a different tenant or portal than the profile targets.
entries.probe: Compare the credential's stored sign-in URL and the screen's branding with the tenant profile's URL, host and path.
entries.recover: Correct the tenant profile mapping, and confirm with the credential's owner which portal it opens.
approaches: Start from the tenant's real sign-in flow
Scout the live screen before writing targets
entries.prevent: Each tenant profile records the sign-in URL proven by a live capture, and each run checks the screen's branding against it.
entries.hazard: proposed: two tenants with the same sign-in look, where one tenant's credential is tried against the other's URL

entries.title: Entry URL shows a shell or landing page, not the sign-in
entries.recognize: The first screen is a blank shell, a landing page or a help page with no credential fields, and the driver stalls or wrongly reports success there.
entries.tell: The start URL is a root or landing URL, or lacks a required tenant path or parameter, and the screen offers only a redirect or a sign-in link.
mistaken_for: A sign-in form that will not render
entries.probe: Record the exact start URL and where it came from, check for a password field, and follow the screen's own sign-in link, noting every host it crosses.
entries.recover: Start from the tenant profile's proven sign-in URL, or follow the screen's own sign-in link, and wait for the credential fields to be fully rendered.
approaches: Start from the tenant's real sign-in flow
Adopt new windows and popups
Scout the live screen before writing targets
entries.prevent: Start URLs come from the tenant profile and are proven by a live capture.
entries.hazard: Blank "Loading" shell at the base URL that redirects after a delay

entries.title: Sign-in form inside a frame
entries.recognize: The top document has no credential fields, while a frame from the sign-in host exists or appears only after a launcher is pressed.
entries.tell: A frame, often from another origin, holds the password field.
entries.probe: List every frame with its URL and title before and after pressing any sign-in launcher, and search each one for a password field.
entries.recover: Resolve the sign-in frame by its origin and drive the form inside it.
approaches: Resolve the sign-in frame by its origin
Start from the tenant's real sign-in flow
Handle splash, gate and consent pages
entries.prevent: Screen capture covers every frame, including frames from other origins.
entries.hazard: Bank 4's sign-in form in a cross-origin iframe

entries.title: Overlay intercepts the pointer
entries.recognize: A press on a field, link or button times out with a report that another element would receive it, or the target is reported not visible.
entries.tell: Something is drawn over the target: a notice bar, a dialog backdrop, a floating label, or a collapsed menu.
entries.probe: Read which element receives the pointer at the target's position, and take a screenshot of the region.
entries.recover: Dismiss the overlay with its decline control, or expand the menu, then re-target and press once.
approaches: Handle splash, gate and consent pages
Dismiss interstitials without enrolling
Take the URL from a link on the screen
entries.prevent: A target must be visible and unobstructed in the screen model before it is pressed.
entries.hazard: proposed: a fixed notice bar drawn over the lower part of the main frame, covering the submit control

entries.title: Driver defect read as a portal problem
entries.recognize: A driver fails the same way on its first live run or on every run, whatever the portal shows, or it signs in and then fails at a step that was never built.
entries.tell: The failure does not depend on the portal: a code error before any screen loads, a stub step, or a target that no live capture contains.
entries.probe: Run the driver against Generic Bank first, check that every target and URL traces to a live capture, and read whether each step is implemented.
entries.recover: Fix the driver from a fresh live capture and prove it on the eval ladder before changing anything else.
approaches: Prove the driver against Generic Bank first
Scout the live screen before writing targets
Single supervised attempt
entries.prevent: Every target and URL in a driver must trace to a saved live capture.

entries.title: Markup changed under a working driver
entries.recognize: A driver that ran cleanly now times out at the same step on every run.
entries.tell: A fresh capture shows the control relabeled or moved, and the last passing run came before the change.
entries.probe: Capture the live screen at the failing step, compare it with the capture from the last passing run, and count failures at the same step.
entries.recover: Classify it as drift, re-scout the screen and repair the driver's targets; do not retry.
approaches: Scout the live screen before writing targets
Visible-only targets
Click the named control by accessible role and name
entries.prevent: A failure that repeats at one step across runs is classified as drift and sent to repair, not retried.
entries.hazard: Vendor upgrade through the UI version setting (relabeled fields, moved buttons)

entries.title: Alarming wording on a working screen taken as the verdict
entries.recognize: An "unavailable" banner, or a word such as "blocked" or "locked", appears while the form keeps working or the expected rows are present, and the driver fails on it.
entries.tell: The banner names another service or comes and goes, or the word sits in help or promotional text, while the content the step needs is on the screen.
mistaken_for: A screen that is not ready
entries.probe: Check for the step's own content before reading any banner, note what the banner names, and find exactly which text the classifier matched.
entries.recover: Classify from the step's own content and the screen's structured messages, not from a word anywhere in the text.
approaches: Poll for content, not the URL or load event
Treat a persistent unavailable state as terminal
Classify before repairing
entries.prevent: Outcome classifiers match messages in their expected place on the screen, never a word anywhere in the page text.
entries.hazard: proposed: a "Bill pay is temporarily unavailable" notice on a working member summary

entries.title: Visible content missing from the document the driver reads
entries.recognize: The screenshot shows a table or control that the driver reports absent, and the top document holds only navigation.
entries.tell: The content lives in an inner frame or a shadow root, not in the top document.
entries.probe: List every frame with its URL and count the rows inside each, and look for the control in the accessibility tree.
entries.recover: Read the frame that holds the content, and build the screen model from every frame and the accessibility tree.
approaches: Read the right frame
Read through shadow roots
Poll for content, not the URL or load event
entries.prevent: The screen model covers every frame and shadow root before any absence verdict.
entries.hazard: Framesets after sign-in, with the work inside the main frame

entries.title: Money-moving control on a screen the driver visits
entries.recognize: Pay, transfer, payee or account-change controls sit on screens the driver visits, near the controls it needs, and a generic Continue can post a change.
entries.tell: The screen's title, headings or form action mention payments, transfers or record changes, or a press would send a write request.
entries.probe: Classify each screen by its title, headings and form actions, and list every write request a press would send, without pressing.
entries.recover: Refuse the press, trip the money-trap guard and let the trip propagate; only a transfer task holding a single-use grant may submit a transfer.
approaches: Money-trap guard
entries.prevent: Read-only sessions refuse every write, and money or account-change controls are blocked unless a grant covers that exact action.
entries.hazard: Money and account-change decoys ("Waive fee", "Add payee", "Pay now")

entries.title: Second factor is not a code the driver can relay
entries.recognize: The code screen asks for an authenticator app, a security key or a passkey, and no code is sent.
entries.tell: The screen names a factor other than a sent code, with or without a link to another method.
entries.probe: Read which factor the screen asks for, and list what any "Try another method" link offers.
entries.recover: Choose a sent-code method when the tenant profile allows one; otherwise hand back for a person to supply the code.
approaches: Reach an authenticator code through another method
Hand back for a person to sign in
entries.hazard: Bank 4's authenticator-style code with no chooser

entries.title: Code confirmed sent but never arrives
entries.recognize: The screen confirms a code was sent, but nothing reaches the inbox, while other mail does.
entries.tell: The send acknowledgement is on the screen, and the delivery path drops or delays mail from that sender.
entries.probe: Confirm the on-screen send acknowledgement, and test the inbox path with a message from the same sender.
entries.recover: Do not request a second code; hand back with a typed result that names the delivery failure.
approaches: Confirmed-send invariant
Pick the delivery channel in the chooser
entries.hazard: proposed: the staff inbox drops or delays an email code after the send acknowledgement

entries.title: Concurrent code challenges cross-wire codes
entries.recognize: With several runs waiting for codes, one fails on a wrong code while another's code is consumed.
entries.tell: Two or more challenges were open at once, and the submitted code came from a message meant for the other one.
entries.probe: List the challenges open at the moment of each answer, and match each submitted code to the message it came from.
entries.recover: Bind each code to one challenge by its sender and send time, and allow one open challenge per operator and tenant.
approaches: Durable code challenge with one owner
entries.prevent: Only one code challenge may be open per operator and tenant at a time.
entries.hazard: proposed: two runs awaiting staff codes for the same operator at the same time

entries.title: Answered code reaches a run that no longer exists
entries.recognize: A person submits a valid code and nothing consumes it; the run sits waiting, or had already been stopped.
entries.tell: The process holding the run restarted or was stopped shortly before the answer, and the run's last log line comes just before it.
entries.probe: Compare the run's last log line, the worker's start time and the time of the answer.
entries.recover: Keep challenges durable with a single owner, and tell the person at once when the run behind a challenge has ended.
approaches: Durable code challenge with one owner
entries.prevent: A challenge whose run has ended is closed and its prompt withdrawn.
